result.title: BunshinRL: Splitting Live Agent Workspaces for Memory-Efficient Agentic RL
result.summary: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) rollouts interleave model reasoning with tool calls in persistent workspaces. Scaling these rollouts incurs substantial memory costs for concurrent environments, while slow tool calls delay entire rollout batches. We present BunshinRL, an agentic RL rollout system that exploits shared environment state and recurring tool calls through three techniques: memory sharing across environments, tool-prefix caching, and speculative tool execution. These techniques build on BunshinFork, a novel live whole-workspace forking mechanism for containers. BunshinFork reconstructs process trees, shares memory copy-on-write, and preserves file, communication, and GUI state, enabling cached-state reuse and rollback after incorrect speculation. We implement BunshinRL and BunshinFork through Linux kernel module and CRIU modifications. BunshinRL reduces peak memory by up to 43%, total memory consumption by up to 51%, and end-to-end rollout latency by 23%.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BunshinRL 这一 agentic RL rollout 系统，通过跨环境内存共享、工具前缀缓存与投机式工具执行，并基于 BunshinFork 的容器级活工作区 fork 降低并发 rollout 的内存占用与延迟。
AI.relevance_reason: 其投机工具执行配合状态快照与错误回滚，可能为 LVR 中「先推测再核验」的 LOOK/STOP 决策与状态回退提供系统层线索，可供核查；但论文关注的是 rollout 基础设施开销，未涉及视觉证据或 latent 表示。
